finding.problem: A previously booked anchor validated at entry could become noncanonical during later recovery/submission reads. A later successor block could overwrite it, or a new intent could use stale prior spending.
finding.fix: Revalidate existing checkpoint after slow reads, before the existing final head/header/fee/day/deadline proofs; no new RPC follows those final proofs.
finding.preserved: same authority, nonce, pending identity, exact fee budget, confirmations, accounting, limits and publication order; anchor-free first nonce adds no RPC
finding.limits: Provider per-call coherence remains trusted; future inclusion and malicious fork switching are not solved by repeated header reads.

follow_through.status: existing boundary, no new defect proven
follow_through.area: Present local JSON parsing has no shared byte-size cap; same-UID/state/config filesystem remains trusted. A cap needs measured maximum long-lived state and explicit compatibility review, not arbitrary defaults.
Advisory flock is not cross-host fencing. Physical disk/power-loss, off-host restore, replacement writer fencing and sustained operating faults need separate acceptance.
Watchdog success means main-process progress, not economic success. Responsive repeated RPC failure requires external stale/error alerting and restart-storm review.

Metadata receipt recovery can need pinned historical getters while the trigger observation is within maximum age. Missing archive/getter availability can delay the serial sender; after the observation ages out its baseline is invalidated. Do not clear pending or resend.
